correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the two spine labels gives three disjoint regimes. In each regime the page constraints were reconstructed from the Roman definition, the only cross-page conditions were identified explicitly, and inclusion-exclusion was applied only to those conditions. Exhaustive direct enumeration for one through five pages agrees with every coefficient and all stated corollaries.

originality.rationale: The closest same-object product theorem covers only the minimum Roman weight. The inspected Roman-polynomial source treats neighboring families and operations but not square books or Cartesian products, while targeted database and own-record searches found no all-weight square-book formula. The known scalar minimum is excluded from the retained originality claim.
residual_risks: Book graphs have multiple naming conventions, so a differently indexed treatment under prism or product terminology may have escaped the searches.
Absence from searched databases is not by itself a novelty proof; PASS rests on statement-level comparison with the closest same-object and same-invariant primary sources.
The general all-parameter formula was not found in the inspected literature, but future bibliographic discovery could alter the originality assessment.

source_inspections.evidence: The paper lists primary MSC 05C69 and states that for a path of order m and a star with at least two leaves the Roman domination number of the Cartesian product is 2m. value.rationale: The polynomial is a natural all-weight refinement of a known scalar product result. It gives every Roman-labeling multiplicity, an exact total count, and a nontrivial change in the number of minimum functions, while the proof isolates a reusable page-factorization mechanism conditioned on the spine labels.
